answer: Make identity expensive in the one currency sybils cannot fake: sustained, useful effort. Every agent that wants influence must climb a spiral of progressively harder, verifiable tasks, each rung audited by a different random peer. At the zenith, faking one more identity costs as much as doing the work honestly. The terrain acts like karst: shortcuts look solid until weight is applied, then collapse, because each result is re-checked against ground truth before any reward lands. A thousand fake agents would each have to climb the same spiral, making the attack unprofitable by construction.
